title: Japan — Northern Alps in autumn
notes: Fifteen nights through the Northern Alps, sequenced north to south and high to low so it follows the autumn colour down the mountain rather than fighting it: the Tateyama range on 12 Oct, Hakuba on 13-15 Oct, Kamikochi on its forecast peak date of 17 Oct, and the Kiso valley last, at around 400 m, where the colour arrives latest. Nothing is booked yet. The weather columns are empty because Open-Meteo only forecasts about 16 days — run tools/fetch_weather.py from late Sep 2027.

summary.note: Budget figures are the whole trip for two travellers, in MYR, and are planning estimates rather than quotes — nothing is booked. They exclude flights. The exchange rate is the mid-market rate on 14 Aug 2026 (1 MYR = 38.9 JPY), a placeholder until money is actually changed; every converted figure on the site moves with it. Day costs carry only fares that have been looked up and checked, so the daily totals are far below what a day will really cost — the planning envelope is this table, not those.

flights.remarks: Not booked. Times are ANA's current timetable as at Aug 2026, held as the planning baseline until the October 2027 schedule loads (usually around 11 months out, so roughly Nov 2026). Waiting on an ANA promotion.

overview.remarks: The Alpine Route, west to east in one day — the traverse is also the transfer to Nagano, so nothing is backtracked. Peak colour today is at Bijodaira and Midagahara on the way up; Murodo at 2,433 m is past its own peak (late Sep) and may well have had its first snow. Dress for near-freezing.

accommodation.remarks: Airport hotel — the flight lands at 22:15, so anything further in is a waste of a night.
Three nights on one base over the holiday weekend, day-tripping to Takayama and the Kurobe Gorge. Near Toyama Station is what matters.
One night, arriving off the last Alpine Route bus from Ogizawa. Onsen ryokan.
Three nights, one base. Ask about laundry — this is the midpoint of the trip.
One night in town, purely so Kamikochi is reachable by late morning.
Book this first. Fewer than ten properties inside the valley and October sells out months ahead. Half board is the norm — there is nowhere else to eat after dark.
Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. A private or semi-open rotenburo is the point of these three nights.
Edo-era minshuku in the post town itself. Most serve dinner and breakfast; several have no televisions, deliberately.

transport.mode: Trains, buses, ropeways and cable cars throughout — no hire car. Private vehicles are banned in Kamikochi, and the Alpine Route is a through ticket across six modes that a car cannot follow.

todo.remarks: Do this first. Fewer than ten properties in the valley and October foliage week sells out months ahead.
Shin-Hotaka or Fukuji. Three nights — worth paying for a private rotenburo on at least one.
Small houses, few rooms each. Book direct or through the Tsumago tourist office.
Three-day holiday weekend and the Takayama festival — book well ahead even though Toyama is a city.
Landing at 22:15 — pick something inside or shuttle-linked to the terminal.
Waiting on an ANA promotion. The Oct 2027 schedule should load around Nov 2026; confirm the times still match before committing the rest.

Murodo runs to around freezing on an October morning and may have had its first snow. Everything else on the trip is far milder — layers, not a second coat.

todo.task: Confirm laundry at the three-night bases
todo.remarks: Toyama, Hakuba and Okuhida. Fifteen nights is too long to pack for otherwise, and a booking rarely states it.
Happo Pond, the Nakasendo and the Murodo paths are all walked, not climbed, but check the policy does not exclude anything above 2,000 m.
